title: Automatic SLI Derivation and Cost-Constrained Trace Capture for Analytics Ingest
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our analytics ingest pipeline produces a wide variety of per-tenant and per-route signals (ingest latency, parse errors, queueing depth, drop rates). Instrument owners keep manually authoring SLIs and choosing sampling policies for traces when things go wrong. That process is slow, error-prone, and leads to poor coverage during short-lived hotspots.

This ticket implements two coordinated capabilities: (1) automatic SLI derivation (ASD) that proposes candidate SLIs from existing metrics and synthetic probes using heuristics and supervised rules, and (2) cost-constrained trace capture (CCTC) — an adaptive, budgeted trace sampling controller that reserves trace capture for signals that matter to derived SLIs and anomalies. The goal is faster SLI onboarding, better signal-to-noise for incidents, and bounded observability cost for analytics ingestion services.
goal: Ship a prototype that can (a) generate and surface suggested SLIs for an ingest service, (b) automatically adjust trace capture rates to prioritize windows with anomalous SLI behavior while honoring a configured cost budget, and (c) provide dashboard templates and runbook links for generated SLIs.
background: We currently rely on hand-curated SLIs and static sampling policies. Several incidents showed we missed short bursts of high error rates because sampling was too low; conversely, some tenants generated disproportionate trace volume. Previous tickets targeted tenant-prioritized throttles and sampling strategies, but none linked synthesized SLIs to dynamic trace routing. This work stitches SLI generation + trace budget enforcement into the ingest observability fabric.
success_metrics: Percentage of ingest regressions detected by ASD-derived SLIs >= 85% on held-out incident set
Reduction in unclassified incident windows requiring manual instrumentation by 50%
Trace storage cost from analytics ingest observability does not exceed configured budget (within +/-10%)
Mean time to link trace to alert reduced by 30% for first-response teams
acceptance_criteria: ASD produces readable SLI suggestions (name, definition, percentile/window) for 90% of ingest routes with non-trivial traffic
Operator can accept/reject and edit a suggested SLI via console before it becomes monitored
CCTC enforces a daily tokenized budget per workspace and emits explainable sampling decisions in logs
End-to-end demo: inject a synthetic parse-error burst -> ASD flags a candidate SLI -> CCTC increases trace sampling for that window -> dashboard shows linked traces within 2 minutes
proposed_design:
1) SLI Derivation: run an offline analyzer over metric timeseries and synthetic probe results to find candidate signals using heuristics: change-point detection, percentile drift, parse-error spike correlation, and request/response tail amplification. Rank candidates by signal-to-noise and potential customer impact. Store suggestions in a suggestion index with provenance metadata.

2) Trace Capture Controller: controller subscribes to suggestion index + live SLI delta stream. It maintains a per-workspace daily cost budget expressed as 'trace tokens'. When an SLI deviates beyond its alert threshold or an anomaly detector flags a window, controller computes a temporary sampling multiplier for affected tenants/routes. Sampling decisions use a reservoir-bucket model: reserved burst tokens for high-priority SLI anomalies, fallback fair-share when budget low. Controller emits sampling decision events to the routing plane and logs decision rationale.

3) UI and Dashboard: Console surfaces suggested SLIs with one-click accept. Dashboard templates are auto-populated for accepted SLIs and include a pane linking sampling events and captured traces. Runbook template suggestions include query snippets for root-cause investigation.

4) Safety: Controller enforces hard upper bound sampling percentage per tenant and circuit-breaker if budget depletion approaches 95% consumption. Audit logs stored for at least 90 days for compliance review.
rollout_plan:
Phase A (internal beta, 2 weeks): run ASD offline, produce suggestions for 10 internal workspaces; run CCTC in read-only mode (no routing changes), emit sampling recommendations to logs and console.

Phase B (pilot, 4 weeks): enable CCTC routing changes for low-risk tenants with a small budget and manual rollback. Monitor costs and coverage.

Phase C (gradual opt-in, 4 weeks): expose opt-in toggles in Console for workspaces; provide migration tooling for existing sampling policies.

Phase D (GA): default to suggestions-only mode; enable auto-sampling only when workspace explicitly opts in or for internal SRE correlation use-cases.
tasks: Design offline ASD analyzer and ranking heuristics
Implement suggestion index and storage schema
Build CCTC controller with token accounting and reservoir buckets
Add decision-explanation events to sampling logs
Integrate routing plane hooks to honor controller decisions
Console UI: suggestion review flow + dashboard templates
Add e2e tests and synthetic incident harness
risks: Incorrect SLI suggestions may cause alert fatigue if not tuned; mitigated by opt-in and human review
Miscalibrated sampling could either overspend trace budget or miss events; mitigated by hard caps and staged rollout
Cross-tenant fairness concerns if high-volume tenants consume burst tokens; mitigated by per-tenant upper bounds and fair-share fallback
open_questions: What heuristics should be used to map metric-level anomalies to trace-capture scopes (tenant vs route vs request-type)?
How to express trace cost budget: tokens per span vs bytes vs retention-cost?
Should accepted ASD SLIs default to active alerting or require explicit enablement?
